title: Length of the Longest Subsequence That Sums to Target
summary: Given an array of integers and a target sum, find the length of the longest subsequence that sums to the target.
statement: Given an array of integers and a target sum, find the length of the longest subsequence that sums to the target. If no such subsequence exists, return -1. A subsequence is derived by removing some or no elements from the original array while maintaining the order of the remaining elements.
constraints: nums contains positive integers and target is positive.
Choose indices in original order whose values sum exactly to target.
Return the maximum chosen length, or -1 when no subsequence reaches target.
hints: For each sum, retain the longest subsequence length achievable from processed items.
Use descending 0-1 knapsack updates so each positive value is considered at most once.
If total-value is reachable, maximize best[total] with best[total-value]+1.
Descending updates preserve the previous-item state, and maximizing length for every exact sum is sufficient for all future extensions.
editorial: Descending updates preserve the previous-item state, and maximizing length for every exact sum is sufficient for all future extensions.

tests.explanation: Both [1,3,5] and [2,3,4] reach nine with maximum length three.
The subsequence [1,3,2,1] reaches seven with length four.
